items.text: Odkiaľ si? = Where are you from? (informal)
items.picture: Emma arrives at the dormitory with a backpack and a suitcase with a shamrock sticker. Lucia, her new roommate, opens the door of their room to her with a welcoming gesture, and asks where she's from.

items.text: Som z Írska. = I'm from Ireland.
items.picture: A green map of Ireland with Emma standing in the middle of it, smiling: this is where she's from.

items.text: Lucia je zo Slovenska. = Lucia is from Slovakia.
items.picture: A green map of Slovakia with Lucia standing on it near Bratislava, smiling: this is where she's from.

items.text: Nemecko, Taliansko, Poľsko = Germany, Italy, Poland
items.picture: Close-up of the map of Europe on the dorm wall, with coloured pins stuck in Germany, Italy and Poland; Emma's hand is pushing in the last one.

items.text: Som z Ukrajiny. = I'm from Ukraine.
items.picture: At the university's international students' evening, Oksana stands at a table decorated with a blue-and-yellow Ukrainian flag and introduces herself, a hand on her chest.

items.text: Som Írka. = I'm Irish. (said by a woman)
items.picture: At the same international evening, Emma stands proudly at the table with the Irish tricolour, a plate of soda bread in front of her.

items.text: Slovák, Slovenka = a Slovak man, a Slovak woman
items.picture: At the international evening, Tomáš and Lucia stand side by side at the table with the Slovak flag, a Slovak man and a Slovak woman, offering little plates of homemade food.

items.text: Ty or vy? Oni or ony?
items.picture: Split picture of two pairs crossing the campus. Left: Lucia and Tomáš walk together, a man and a woman. Right: Lucia and Emma walk together, two women.

items.text: You ask your teacher, pani Horváthová, where she is from. What do you say?
items.picture: After class, Emma stands at pani Horváthová's desk and asks her something politely; the teacher, packing up her books, turns to answer with a smile.

items.text: Pán Kováč speaks very fast and you don't understand. What do you say?
items.picture: At the dormitory's front desk, Emma checks in with her passport in hand. Pán Kováč, typing at the computer, asks her something very fast; Emma looks lost and apologetic.

items.text: Koľko máš rokov? = How old are you? (informal)
items.picture: In the dorm common room, Marek lounges in an armchair with his hands behind his head; Emma, sitting forward on a chair, asks him with a teasing smile how old he is.

items.text: Mám dvadsaťpäť rokov. = I'm twenty-five.
prvý, druhý, tretí = first, second, third
items.picture: After a university fun run, Tomáš, Lucia and Emma stand on a winners' podium: Tomáš on the top step, Lucia second, Emma third, all laughing and out of breath.

items.text: Haló? = Hello? (on the phone)
items.picture: Split picture of a phone call. Left: in the dorm room, Lucia picks up her ringing phone and answers, curious who it is. Right: Emma calls her from a street in the Old Town, smiling.

items.text: Tu je Emma. = It's Emma. (on the phone)
Your phone rings and you pick it up. What do you say?
telefonovať = to phone, to be on the phone
items.picture: Tomáš leans back in his office chair with his feet up on his untidy desk, chatting away on the phone and waving his free hand as he talks.

items.text: telefónne číslo = phone number
items.picture: After class, in the corridor outside the classroom, Oksana asks Emma for her phone number and types it into her phone as Emma reads it out.

items.text: Aké máš telefónne číslo? = What's your phone number? (informal)
Zavolám ti. = I'll call you.
items.picture: Evening at a tram stop: Lucia, stepping onto the tram, turns in the doorway and holds a hand to her ear like a phone; Emma, staying behind on the platform, nods and waves.

items.text: Dopočutia! = Goodbye! (on the phone)
items.picture: Emma, at her desk in the dorm room, finishes a phone call: she says goodbye with a warm smile and takes the phone from her ear to hang up.

items.text: You meet a new teacher for the first time. How do you ask her name?
